subject: Private endpoint egress: proposed NAT binding + 'egress stapling' plan
body:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@orionhealth.com>, orion-infra@orionhealth.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress: proposed NAT binding + 'egress stapling' plan

Hi Alice / Orion infra team,

Following our architecture review yesterday, attaching the diagram and a spreadsheet that enumerates the proposed static NAT pools and ports we'd like to bind for the Redwood private endpoint deployed into your VPC. High level proposal:

- Provide a dedicated static NAT IP pool per-region (three ranges in us-east-1/us-west-2/us-west-1) that traffic from the private endpoint will egress from.
- Support two operational modes:
  1) Direct static IP allowlist - we guarantee outbound connections originate from the static NAT IPs in the sheet.
  2) Proxy + stapling - for customers who want richer attribution/auditability we can route egress through a Redwood-managed outbound proxy that inserts a short-lived signed header (what we're calling an "egress stapling") so you can map sessions back to the underlying customer session in your observability stack. This avoids full TLS termination at the perimeter while still enabling per-request audit IDs.

Questions for Orion infra to action:
1) Can you confirm whether you will accept mode (1) static-IP allowlisting only, or if you want us to onboard the proxy + stapling (mode 2)?
2) If mode (1): please confirm which ACL apply (firewall vendor / next-hop) and any required ticketing SLA for IP changes.
3) If mode (2): we will need your security team's input on header acceptance policy (we use a signed JWT in X-Redwood-Egress-Auth, TTL=5m).
4) Any constraints around TLS inspection or mandated MITM for outbound traffic (this affects our recommendation).

Attachments: orion-network-diagram.pdf (logical layout), orion-egress-nat-pools.xlsx (proposed CIDRs/IPs).

Next step: if you can reply with mode preference and a contact in your firewall/edge team we'll publish a final cutover checklist.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@orionhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: orion-infra@orionhealth.com, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:35:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: proposed NAT binding + 'egress stapling' plan

Thanks, Mina. Quick clarifications from our side:
- We prefer static IPs where possible (mode 1) due to audit controls and our inability to accept custom headers at the perimeter today.
- TLS interception is not permitted for any customer traffic; we can only allow bifurcation where AWS VPC Gateway Endpoints exist (S3, KMS, Secrets Manager).
- For third-party endpoints (downstream telemetry, spikes, external model hosts), we'll need fully enumerated IPs/FQDNs and an administrative contact for change windows.

Action: I'll work with our firewall team and come back with a list of the specific ACL objects we can use (vendor: Palo Alto). Expected by: Mon 2 Nov EOD.

Alice Jenkins
Network Engineering, Orion Health
